## Structure and components

- [statement] SynNeurGe links its biological components to a clinical component C, defined by either a single high-specificity feature or multiple lower-specificity clinical features. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The Movement Disorder Society task-force critique describes Hoehn–Yahr as nonlinear and heavily weighted toward postural instability, with incomplete coverage of other motor disability and no information on nonmotor problems. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15372591/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] In its report, the Movement Disorder Society task force recommended the original Hoehn–Yahr form for demographic group descriptions, reporting medians and ranges, and nonparametric analysis of changes; it reported no clinimetric data then available for the widely adopted half-stage modification. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15372591/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] Braak’s proposed pattern does not apply to every patient: the 2017 review limits its staging fit to a subset with young onset and long disease duration, while the 2008 critical evaluation reports exceptions and neurologically intact people with extensive postmortem pathology. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/
- [statement] Höglinger and Lang explicitly distinguish SynNeurGe classification from staging: they refrained from proposing disease stages pending prospective evidence establishing temporal order; NSD-ISS is a separate staging proposal. (low confidence) — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1877718X241298194 · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/biological-definition-parkinsons-disease-two-proposals-pave-way
- [statement] In their 2024 comparison, Höglinger and Lang classify an isolated S-positive result without confirmed neurodegeneration as Parkinson’s/Lewy-type synucleinopathy, whereas they describe NSD-ISS as assigning such individuals stage 1A; they dispute treating this finding alone as a clinical disease diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1877718X241298194 · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] The Braak pathological sequence is not universal across patients or Lewy-body disorders; reviews describe nonconforming distributions, so it should not be assumed to represent every patient’s disease course. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full
- [statement] Burke and colleagues cautioned that Braak pathological stages cannot be directly equated with clinical severity or inevitable future clinical Parkinson’s disease: their review describes advanced pathological stages in neurologically unimpaired individuals and no relationship with clinical severity in the data examined. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] SynNeurGe’s proposed biological classification has three components: pathological α-synuclein in tissues or CSF (S), imaging evidence of neurodegeneration (N), and pathogenic variants that cause or strongly predispose to Parkinson’s disease (G). (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/biological-definition-parkinsons-disease-two-proposals-pave-way
- [statement] Published interpretations differ: an autopsy-based study concluded that the PD staging scheme is valid except in the setting of advanced Alzheimer’s disease, whereas Burke and colleagues judged the evidence insufficient to establish the proposed caudal-to-rostral temporal progression of human Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20187227/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/
- [statement] In an analysis of PPMI, PASADENA and SPARK data published in npj Parkinson's Disease in 2024, 1741 participants had SAA data and 1030 (59%) were S+ consistent with neuronal alpha-synuclein disease (NSD); among sporadic PD, 683/736 (93%) were NSD, with a baseline distribution across NSD-ISS Stages 2B, 3 and 4 of 25%, 63% and 9%. The authors state that validation of the proposed anchors in longitudinal cohorts is necessary. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00789-w · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Braak staging proposes a neuropathological sequence beginning in lower-brainstem or olfactory structures, proceeding toward substantia nigra involvement and eventually cortex; the proposed direction of spread is a hypothesis rather than a clinical disability score. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20187227/
- [statement] Braak’s six-pattern scheme inferred temporal progression from progressively broader postmortem distributions of abnormal α-synuclein staining; in that proposed sequence substantia-nigra involvement appears around stage 3, rather than at its earliest stage. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Hoehn–Yahr stage 1 describes unilateral involvement; stage 2 describes bilateral or midline involvement without impaired balance. (medium confidence) — https://www.physio-pedia.com/Hoehn_and_Yahr_Scale · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/stages
- [statement] Hoehn–Yahr stage three is marked by impaired balance and mild-to-moderate disability, while the person remains physically capable of independent living. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/stages · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.physio-pedia.com/Hoehn_and_Yahr_Scale
- [statement] Hoehn–Yahr stage 4 denotes severe disability with standing or walking still possible unassisted; stage 5 denotes confinement to a bed or wheelchair unless aided. (medium confidence) — https://www.physio-pedia.com/Hoehn_and_Yahr_Scale · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/stages
- [statement] SynNeurGe classifies pathological α-synuclein (S), neurodegeneration (N), and pathogenic genetic variants (G), linked to clinical manifestations (C); these are biological classification dimensions. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1877718X241298194
- [statement] The 2024 SynNeurGe proposal specifies initial use exclusively for research and acknowledges ethical implications, limitations and the need for prospective validation. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/biological-definition-parkinsons-disease-two-proposals-pave-way
- [statement] Braak and colleagues interpreted increasingly extensive, nested pathological distributions as a temporal sequence: stage 1 involved medulla or olfactory structures, stage 2 added rostrally adjacent brainstem structures, and stages 3–4 were proposed to coincide with substantia nigra neuron loss and clinical parkinsonism. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
